subject.title: [Feature]: Compaction: configurable model override + flush-then-reset mode

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in success-path mode that resets a session immediately after a successful agentic memory flush instead of running compaction, and what config, consent, timeout, audit, and security boundaries should govern it?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the remaining behavior changes silent model execution, provider routing, session-state retention, and privacy/security semantics, so automation should not choose the policy alone.

options.title: Design bounded reset-after-flush
options.body: Approve an explicit opt-in mode with timeout, duplicate-reset protection, durable-memory expectations, user/audit visibility, and security constraints before implementation.

options.title: Fold into reset-memory policy
options.body: Track the remaining behavior under the open reset-memory issue so reset-time and flush-time session rotation share one lifecycle contract.

options.title: Keep compaction as recovery path
options.body: Decline automatic reset-after-flush and keep the current model overrides plus compaction/exhaustion recovery behavior as the supported path.

recommendation.title: Design bounded reset-after-flush
recommendation.body: Approve an explicit opt-in mode with timeout, duplicate-reset protection, durable-memory expectations, user/audit visibility, and security constraints before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the closest current-main memory-flush reset recovery behavior and is the strongest available owner for the cross-boundary lifecycle decision.
